</section></div></div></div><div class="accordion-list-item-container multi-accrodion"><div class="accordion-item-header"><a data-accordion-all-device="true" data-open="false" class="accordion-trigger contains-heading accordion-closed" role="button" data-accordion-use-cookie="true" data-accordion-body="#accord-1-2" aria-controls="accord-1-2" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0"><i aria-hidden="true"></i><h2 class="item-text">Code of Meeting Practice</h2></a></div><div class="accordion-item-body multi-accordion-body clearfix rs_skip" id="accord-1-2" style="display: none;"><div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>The elected councillors meet at Council Meetings and Committee Meetings in accordance with Council’s <a title="Code-of-Meeting-Practice-June-2026.pdf" href="/files/assets/public/v/2/council/council-meetings/code-of-meeting-practice-july-2026.pdf" target="_self" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Code of Meeting Practice<span class="file-info">(PDF, 397KB)</span></a>.</p>
<p>Under section 360(2) of the Local Government Act Council may establish a Code of Meeting Practice.  The Code must incorporate meeting procedures set out in the Local Government Act 1993 and Local Government (General) Regulation 2005 and can incorporate local provisions.  However, in adopting local provisions, the Code must be consistent with the relevant legislative provisions.  Council and Committee meetings must operate in accordance with the adopted Code of Meeting Practice.</p>
<p> </p>
</div></div></div><div class="accordion-list-item-container multi-accrodion"><div class="accordion-item-header"><a data-accordion-all-device="true" data-open="false" class="accordion-trigger contains-heading accordion-closed" role="button" data-accordion-use-cookie="true" data-accordion-body="#accord-1-3" aria-controls="accord-1-3" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0"><i aria-hidden="true"></i><h2 class="item-text">Public Forum</h2></a></div><div class="accordion-item-body multi-accordion-body clearfix rs_skip" id="accord-1-3" style="display: none;"><div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>Council conducts an Public Forum session during Council Meetings which is limited to fifteen (15) minutes. A person or persons may address Council only on matters on the agenda of the meeting. Speakers can request to speak by completing the ‘Request to Address Council or Committee Meetings’ form or make a request to speak during the Public Forum session.</p>
<p>Speakers are limited to five minutes.  Speakers can speak on matters other than those listed on the evening’s business papers, those matters being actioned under Council’s complaints handling mechanisms, in dispute or under investigation or a Code of Conduct complaint or investigation.</p>
<p> </p>
</div></div></div><div class="accordion-list-item-container multi-accrodion"><div class="accordion-item-header"><a data-accordion-all-device="true" data-open="false" class="accordion-trigger contains-heading accordion-closed" role="button" data-accordion-use-cookie="true" data-accordion-body="#accord-1-4" aria-controls="accord-1-4" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0"><i aria-hidden="true"></i><h2 class="item-text">Who can speak at Council Meetings?</h2></a></div><div class="accordion-item-body multi-accordion-body clearfix rs_skip" id="accord-1-4" style="display: none;"><div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>Members of the public may attend Council and Committee Meetings and may speak on matters, such as those in general business on the agenda of the meeting.</p>
<p>To speak at a meeting please complete the below Request to Address Council Meeting form. Requests to address a meeting must be submitted in writing by 12.00pm on the day of the meeting to the General Manager. Speakers are limited to five minutes and must provide their name and address to the meeting. Speakers are not permitted to ask questions of Councillors or staff.</p>
<p><a title="Request-to-Address-Council-Committee-Meetings.pdf" href="/files/assets/public/v/1/council/council-meetings/request-to-address-council-committee-meetings_1.pdf" target="_self" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Request to Address Council Committee Meetings.pdf<span class="file-info">(PDF, 162KB)</span></a></p>
<p> </p>
</div></div></div><div class="accordion-list-item-container multi-accrodion"><div class="accordion-item-header"><a data-accordion-all-device="true" data-open="false" class="accordion-trigger contains-heading accordion-closed" role="button" data-accordion-use-cookie="true" data-accordion-body="#accord-1-5" aria-controls="accord-1-5" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0"><i aria-hidden="true"></i><h2 class="item-text">Are there restrictions on what I can speak about?</h2></a></div><div class="accordion-item-body multi-accordion-body clearfix rs_skip" id="accord-1-5" style="display: none;"><div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>Speakers are limited to a maximum of four (4) on an item and speak on an alternative basis eg commencing with a speaker for, then a speaker against. Additional speakers may be permitted by decision of the Council meeting.</p>
<p>Speakers have a time limit of 5 minutes each and can only speak once in the course of the meeting. Members of the public address Council prior to debate by Councillors.</p>
<p>On occasion, a council or committee meeting may be closed to the public when matters listed in Section 14.1 of the Code are discussed. This can include legal advices, matters relating to commercial information or trade secret, or personnel hardship of a resident. Section 14.9 may allow representations by members of the public prior to the meeting closing to the public.</p>
<p>Council webcasts and records proceedings at Council and Committee meetings, which includes speeches of members of the public. The purpose of recording the meeting is to assist in preparation of meetings minutes, which is the official record of Council and Committee Meetings.  It is prohibited to privately record, by visual and audio recording devices, Council or Committee meetings without permission of the Council.</p>
<p> </p>
</div></div></div><div class="accordion-list-item-container multi-accrodion"><div class="accordion-item-header"><a data-accordion-all-device="true" data-open="false" class="accordion-trigger contains-heading accordion-closed" role="button" data-accordion-use-cookie="true" data-accordion-body="#accord-1-6" aria-controls="accord-1-6" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0"><i aria-hidden="true"></i><h2 class="item-text">Conduct of the Meeting</h2></a></div><div class="accordion-item-body multi-accordion-body clearfix rs_skip" id="accord-1-6" style="display: none;"><div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>All participants at Council meetings including Councillors, Council staff and members of the public are expected not to make personal comments concerning Councillors, staff or other members of the public or engage in disorderly conduct at a meeting. Acts of disorder are outlined in Section 15.12 of the Code. Penalties for disorder may include rescinding speaking rights or expulsion from the meeting.</p>
<p>These guidelines relate to Council’s Code of Meeting Practice. The Code is made under Local Government Act 1993 and Local Government Regulations. The Code is also available to view at Council’s Customer Service Centre.</p>
<p> </p>
</div></div></div><div class="accordion-list-item-container multi-accrodion"><div class="accordion-item-header"><a data-accordion-all-device="true" data-open="false" class="accordion-trigger contains-heading accordion-closed" role="button" data-accordion-use-cookie="true" data-accordion-body="#accord-1-7" aria-controls="accord-1-7" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0"><i aria-hidden="true"></i><h2 class="item-text">Business Papers</h2></a></div><div class="accordion-item-body multi-accordion-body clearfix rs_skip" id="accord-1-7" style="display: none;"><div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>Business papers, minutes and agendas are available below for 2020 meetings, with past meetings available at the bottom link.</p>
<p>Council Meetings are open to the public, except for discussion of legal, staff or other confidential matters</p>
<p>Before each Council or Committee meeting, a Business Paper is prepared detailing the items that are to be presented to the meeting.  Business papers include an agenda (list of items to be considered at the meeting), reports (details of items to be considered by Council) and minutes (details of decisions made at previous Council and Committee meetings).</p>
<p>Readers should be aware that the Recommendations as set out in the Business Papers are simply proposals to the Council for its consideration. The Council may adopt these proposals, amend the proposals, determine a completely different course of action, or it may decline to pursue any course of action. The decision of the Council becomes a resolution of the Council and is recorded in the Minutes.</p>
<p>Ordinary meetings of Council are held on the first Tuesday of the month, except during January and July. Business papers for the Council meetings are published on the Council website on the Thursday prior to the Tuesday meeting. Copies may be viewed on a computer at Council’s libraries and copies of the report will be printed upon request.</p>
<p>Minutes of the Council Meetings are placed on Council’s website within five working days of the meeting. For further information on Council and Committee meeting agendas, minutes or business papers please contact Council’s Governance department on 9748 9999.</p>
<p> </p>
</div></div></div><div class="accordion-list-item-container multi-accrodion"><div class="accordion-item-header"><a data-accordion-all-device="true" data-open="false" class="accordion-trigger contains-heading accordion-closed" role="button" data-accordion-use-cookie="true" data-accordion-body="#accord-1-8" aria-controls="accord-1-8" aria-expanded="false" tabindex="0"><i aria-hidden="true"></i><h2 class="item-text">Congratulatory Letters</h2></a></div><div class="accordion-item-body multi-accordion-body clearfix rs_skip" id="accord-1-8" style="display: none;"><div class="oc-wysiwyg-container-panel-content">
<p>Strathfield Council offers a range of congratulatory messages from Council to residents who are celebrating significant milestones in their lives.</p>
<p>Some examples where residents may be eligible for a congratulatory message include:</p>
<ul>
    <li>90 or 100th birthdays or any birthday after turning 90</li>
    <li>50 or 60th wedding anniversaries or any anniversary after 50</li>
    <li>being nominated for a significant community award</li>
    <li>winning a significant community award</li>
</ul>
<p>To nominate a community member for a congratulatory message from the Mayor please complete and send in the form below.</p>
<p>Council also offers letters of condolence to those who have recently been diagnosed with a serious illness or have passed away. For more information contact Council on 9748 9999 email <a href="mailto:council@strathfield.nsw.gov.au">council@strathfield.nsw.gov.au</a></p>
<p>Australians can also apply for messages from the Prime Minister, Governor General and the Queen. To do this, you must contact the local Federal Member or any office of any Senator. More information about this can be found <a href="https://www.pmc.gov.au/government/its-honour" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" aria-describedby="new-window-0" class="opens-in-new-tab">here.</a></p>
<p><a title="Congratulatory-Letter-Application.pdf" href="/files/assets/public/v/1/council/council-meetings/congratulatory-letter-application_1.pdf" target="_self" class="document ext-pdf"><i aria-hidden="true"></i>Congratulatory Letter Application.pdf<span class="file-info">(PDF, 80KB)</span></a></p>
<p> </p>
</div></div></div></div></div>

<h2></h2>
<h4><span style="font-size: 1.7778em;">Local Transport Forum</span></h4>
<p>The Local Transport Forum meets regularly through the year to review potential changes in traffic and parking management on local roads within the Strathfield LGA. The Forum is comprised of representatives of from Transport for NSW, Strathfield Council, NSW Police and a representative from the local State Member for Parliament.  Council also consults with bus operators where bus services may be impacted.</p>
<p><span style="font-size: 1em;">The Forum operates under the following delegation from Transport for NSW:  </span><a href="https://aus01.safelinks.protection.outlook.com/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.transport.nsw.gov.au%2Fsystem%2Ffiles%2Fmedia%2Fdocuments%2F2025%2F2025-Authorisation-Delegation-Instrument.pdf&data=05%7C02%7Cayla.karabulut%40strathfield.nsw.gov.au%7C81bd4cefd9624e49db3408ddf022832b%7Cdfcb3a8506bf4fdb9a7443f3f93a1f85%7C1%7C0%7C638930753226279980%7CUnknown%7CTWFpbGZsb3d8eyJFbXB0eU1hcGkiOnRydWUsIlYiOiIwLjAuMDAwMCIsIlAiOiJXaW4zMiIsIkFOIjoiTWFpbCIsIldUIjoyfQ%3D%3D%7C0%7C%7C%7C&sdata=tYu97tvXJ%2BUqiCysxyJehkGFMUnLUeN5WyLhNUmBWaQ%3D&reserved=0" style="font-size: 1em;">2025 Authorisation Delegation Instrument for Councils</a><span style="font-size: 1.125em;"> </span></p>
<p><span style="font-size: 1em;">The meetings are typically held on 11.00am – 12.30pm (on the 3rd</span><em style="font-size: 1em;"></em><span style="font-size: 1em;">Tuesday of the Month).</span></p>
